TRV.name: Travelers Companies, Inc.
kill_criteria: Consolidated combined ratio > 95% for two consecutive quarters (vs 83.6% in Q2 2026)
Net favorable prior-year reserve development flips to net adverse in Business Insurance or Bond & Specialty for two consecutive quarters
Core ROE < 12% for two consecutive quarters (vs ~19-25% now)
Personal Insurance underlying combined ratio rises back above ~90%
A single catastrophe/accumulation net of reinsurance exceeding ~15-20% of shareholders' equity (>$5-6.6B on $33.1B equity)
key_adverse_facts: ~6.7 of the 6.7-point YoY consolidated combined-ratio improvement in Q2 2026 (90.3%->83.6%) is attributable to lower catastrophe losses and higher reserve releases (base effect from the January 2025 California Palisades/Eaton wildfires), not underlying pricing improvement; underlying combined ratio was essentially flat (84.7%->84.1%)
Bond & Specialty segment underlying combined ratio worsened 1.6-2.5 points YoY in 2026
Net favorable prior-year reserve development running at elevated levels (~$991M pre-tax 1H2026 vs $693M 1H2025), a real earnings tailwind that is not assured to continue
Average EPS surprise +57.9% over the last 8 quarters (d4) is an unusually large and likely unstable magnitude, driven by the same cat/reserve base effects rather than durable estimate-beating skill
Long-standing asbestos & environmental legacy claims exposure disclosed (10-Q Note 15) - monitored for decades, no new deterioration this quarter but a perpetual tail risk
data_conflicts: lead_prelim_rank.csv debt_lt+debt_st = $6.161B materially understates TRV's own reported total debt of $9.068B (Q2 2026) / $9.267B (FY2025) per the company's debt-to-capital reconciliation table - a ~32% ($2.9B) understatement, likely because the quant pipeline's debt tag misses part of TRV's long-term debt stack. Affects the leverage factor input to the Q family score.

confidence_in_thesis.reason: Very rich, internally consistent primary-source data (10-Q, 8-K press release + financial supplement, XBRL) with a clean, well-evidenced cyclicality finding (underlying combined ratio flat while recorded ratio swings on cat/reserve base effects). Confidence is not 'high' because the magnitude of the coming 2027 comp reset is not yet fully knowable and one segment (Bond & Specialty) already shows genuine underlying deterioration.

ALL.name: The Allstate Corporation
kill_criteria: Property-Liability recorded combined ratio > 100% for two consecutive quarters
Auto or homeowners policies-in-force growth turns negative for two consecutive quarters

Adjusted net income ROE (ttm) falls below ~15% (confirms hard mean reversion) OR stays >35% for two more quarters without a corresponding upward revision to FY2027 consensus (denial rather than resolution of the air-pocket)
Net favorable reserve development flips negative in auto/casualty for two consecutive quarters
Homeowners underlying combined ratio deteriorates a further ~5 points from 61.5%
key_adverse_facts: d4 quant snapshot explicitly flags ntm_flags='fy1_below_fy0_by_15pct+', ntm_quality='caution': FY2027 consensus EPS ($27.74) is 21.3% below FY2026 consensus ($35.26) - the largest forward-EPS air-pocket of the three names
Trailing adjusted net income ROE (ttm) is 44.2%, up from 28.6% a year ago - a magnitude the sector playbook itself calls 'excellent and rare' at 15%+, i.e. this is a cyclical peak, not a run-rate

Underlying (ex-cat, ex-reserve-development) homeowners combined ratio actually WORSENED to 61.5% from ~58.6% YoY ('reflecting higher loss costs') even as the recorded ratio improved sharply on lower catastrophe losses - a genuine deterioration masked by a benign-cat headline

~9.9 of the 9.9-point YoY 1H2026 consolidated combined-ratio improvement (94.2%->84.3%) is mostly catastrophe base effect (January 2025 California wildfires) and reserve releases; underlying combined ratio improved only 1.5 points
Book value per share +49.7% YoY - an extraordinary, unrepeatable one-year jump, not a steady-state compounding rate
FY2022 net income was -$1.289B (per XBRL), a reminder of how severe the personal-auto downside can be when the pricing cycle turns against the company
data_conflicts: None material found for ALL's debt figures (b1 prelim $7.742B, Yahoo/d4 $7.497B, company-reported $7.492B are all reasonably consistent) - contrast with TRV and GL where debt fields conflict materially with primary filings

PGR (cited as a peer) shows pe_ntm = 0.27 in d4_live_snapshot.parquet, which is almost certainly a data anomaly (denominator/split artefact) and was excluded from the valuation comparison rather than used

confidence_in_thesis.reason: Data is rich and internally consistent, and the cyclicality finding is unusually well-evidenced (explicit d4 flag + primary-source combined-ratio decomposition agree). Confidence is capped at 'medium' rather than 'high' because the INCLUDE-SMALL call requires judging where normalized ROE ultimately settles (high-teens vs. mid-single-digits), which cannot be resolved from filings alone - it depends on how the personal-auto pricing cycle plays out over the next several quarters. Could not fetch the ALL Q4/FY2025 earnings release directly (persistent SEC EDGAR 503s this session); FY2024/FY2025 annuals used XBRL company facts instead, a fully primary but less narrative-rich source.

GL.name: Globe Life Inc.
kill_criteria: Full-year net operating EPS guidance is CUT (not just a smaller raise) versus the prior quarter's range
Consolidated Company Action Level RBC ratio falls below ~280% (vs 316% for 2025, target band 300-320%)
Adverse class-certification ruling or a settlement/verdict in the City of Miami Matter exceeding roughly 5% of shareholders' equity (~$310M on $6.16B equity)
Life or health underwriting margin growth turns negative for two consecutive quarters at any major division
Net operating ROE ex-AOCI falls below ~12% (vs 14.3% 1H2026)
Disclosure of a formal DOJ/SEC enforcement action or order (escalation from the current no-mention status)
key_adverse_facts: A consolidated federal securities class action (City of Miami Gen. Emp. & Sanitation Emp. Ret. Trust v. Globe Life Inc., E.D. Tex., Case No. 4:24-cv-00376), derived from the April 2024 Fuzzy Panda/Viceroy short-seller reports alleging fraudulent policy issuance, forged signatures and unauthorized customer bank withdrawals at American Income Life, remains fully unresolved and reached the class-certification-motion stage on 2026-05-15 (10-Q Note 5) - this is exactly the kind of adverse fact the prior v3 process was found to have omitted

The alleged misconduct centers on the agent-recruitment/sales-practice engine that IS Globe Life's entire distribution model, creating a harder-to-quantify reputational/recruiting risk beyond any monetary judgment
FY2026 guidance growth is decelerating even while beating and raising: current midpoint ($15.75) implies only +8.5% YoY vs FY2025's actual +17.4% YoY growth
Stock-based compensation grew 74% over two years (FY2023 $30.7M -> FY2025 $53.4M) - still immaterial (~0.9% of revenue) but the fastest-growing of the three names
Capex grew 5x from FY2022 ($27.9M) to FY2025 ($142.5M) - absolute level still small but the trend was not independently explained in this pass
data_conflicts: Yahoo/d4 y_totalDebt for GL is $3.427B, roughly 70-80% higher than the actual senior-notes-plus-junior-subordinated-debentures book value of approximately $1.9-2.0B per the Q2 2026 10-Q fair-value table. The b1 prelim csv's own debt_lt ($1.630B) is actually closer to the true figure than Yahoo's - a generic screen using the Yahoo debt field would materially overstate GL's leverage.

confidence_in_thesis.reason: Financial-statement and guidance-execution evidence is unusually clean and fully primary-sourced (four consecutive verified guidance raises with exact prior ranges, RBC ratio disclosed, debt fully reconciled). Confidence is capped at 'medium' rather than 'high' solely because of genuine, irreducible uncertainty in the outstanding securities litigation: the Q2 2026 10-Q contains no DOJ/SEC mention and a July 2025 secondary source described the probes as winding down, but that secondary source was paywalled beyond the headline and could not be independently verified in full, and the securities class action itself is still live and unresolved.

cross_cutting_findings: For all three insurers, the pre-registered quant model's generic Quality/Value factor inputs (gross-profit/assets, EBIT/EV, generic leverage, raw trailing ROE/earnings yield) are, per the finance-skills insurance sector playbook, undefined or misleading for underwriters; the Q/V scores for TRV and ALL in particular are substantially driven by trailing GAAP ROE currently inflated by a shared catastrophe base effect (January 2025 Southern California Palisades/Eaton wildfires) and elevated prior-year reserve releases, not by a structural change in business quality. This should be corrected or at minimum flagged before the b1_live_scores.csv run treats these scores at face value for insurers.

TRV and ALL both show the same mechanism: large YoY 'recorded' combined-ratio improvement almost entirely explained by lower catastrophe losses (base effect vs. the Jan-2025 CA wildfire quarter) and higher reserve releases, while the underlying (ex-cat, ex-reserve-development) combined ratio is flat-to-slightly-worse. This directly confirms the D4 flag questioning whether current earnings are cyclically elevated for P&C names, and explains why sell-side FY2027 EPS consensus is already below FY2026 for both (ALL -21.3%, TRV -15.95% eps_growth_ntm_vs_ttm).

GL is a genuinely different risk profile from TRV/ALL: its earnings are life/health-programmatic rather than P&C-cyclical, and d4 shows no forward EPS air-pocket for GL - its main risk is idiosyncratic (litigation), not cyclical.

Debt fields in the shared quant pipeline (lead_prelim_rank.csv) and in the Yahoo-sourced d4_live_snapshot.parquet disagree with primary filings in different directions for two of the three names (TRV: prelim understates; GL: Yahoo overstates), which would distort any leverage-based screening or risk-capacity calculation for insurers specifically - worth a targeted data-quality fix given how leverage-sensitive the sector is.
